summary.one_liner: Community-maintained repository of content behind roadmap.sh, a set of learning roadmaps, best-practice guides and question sets for developers and tech roles.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a directory of roadmaps covering frontend, backend, DevOps, cloud, AI/ML, data, languages, frameworks, databases, security, design and management paths, with beginner variants for some. It also lists interactive best-practice guides (backend and frontend performance, code review, API security, AWS) and question sets for JavaScript, Node.js, React, backend and frontend. Roadmap nodes are interactive on the website, where clicking a node opens more detail on that topic. In this repository, each markdown file holds the content for one topic, and the node id in the file name links it to the roadmap. Merged changes are synced to the website automatically. The README also points to a scripts folder with maintainer sync tooling and to contribution docs.
use_cases: Choosing a learning path for a developer career
Finding a step-by-step topic list for a language or framework
Reviewing performance or API security best practices
Contributing topic content to community roadmaps
notable: Covers a very wide range of roadmaps, from HTML and Git to AI agents, Kubernetes and Cyber Security
Each topic is a markdown file whose node id links it to the interactive roadmap
Includes best-practice guides and question sets alongside the roadmaps
Content is synced automatically to the roadmap.sh website after merges
caveats: The README does not describe a runnable application; the repository holds content that powers the roadmap.sh website
Maintainer sync tooling is documented separately in scripts/readme.md, which was not part of the provided text
License is only referenced by a license file; the name is not stated in the README
